page: OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor from the Haswell family, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz without TSX support. The configuration provides 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, paired with 60.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline speed of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom-25% results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with middle-50% scores in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance follows a similar pattern: read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks is average, but large-block write bandwidth falls into the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density, the instance offers stable multi-core execution for workloads that do not require high single-threaded clock speeds. Average performance in Passmark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput indicates suitability for multi-threaded web servers, database hosting, and software compilation. However, the hardware profile is less efficient for heavy single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation, where the medium 7B model text generation speed is weak.
description: The OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical Intel cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, 60.0 GB of RAM, a 400 GB local SSD, and 1 Gbps network bandwidth. Benchmark data reveals a performance tradeoff: single-core execution and large-block memory write bandwidth are weak, falling into the bottom 25% of tested systems. Conversely, multi-core performance, read-only memory bandwidth, and software compilation capabilities reach average levels. This resource density makes the server qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads such as database operations, static web serving, and parallelized build systems, while it remains less suited for single-threaded processing or complex large language model text generation.
